Interaction Effect Size between Baseline Insulin Resistance Status and Peak Glucose Reduction (Protein vs Fiber Preload in Rice Experiments)

Using a linear mixed-effects model (random intercept per subject) on 19 participants with both Rice+Fiber and Rice+Protein conditions and SSPG data:

The interaction coefficient (mitigator[Protein] × SSPG) = 0.170 (SE = 0.064, z = 2.652, p = 0.008, 95% CI: [0.044, 0.295]).

This means: for every 1-unit increase in SSPG (mg/dL), the protein-vs-fiber preload effect on peak glucose changes by +0.170 mg/dL. The effect direction is that higher insulin resistance (higher SSPG) reduces or reverses the beneficial glucose-lowering effect of protein preload.

Standardized effect sizes:
- Standardized beta (z-score regression): -0.541 (95% CI: [-0.971, -0.111])
- Pearson r(SSPG, peak_reduction) = -0.541, p = 0.017
- Spearman rho = -0.502, p = 0.029
- Cohen's f² = 0.414 (large effect by Cohen's 1988 conventions)

Crossover point: Protein preload switches from beneficial to detrimental at SSPG ≈ 146 mg/dL. Insulin-sensitive individuals (SSPG < 146) show lower peak glucose with protein vs fiber preload; insulin-resistant individuals (SSPG > 146) paradoxically show higher peak glucose with protein preload.

HOMA-IR interaction was not significant (β = 2.47, p = 0.404), consistent with SSPG (whole-body clamp-derived IR) being the more physiologically relevant measure for postprandial glucose disposal.

**Summary of findings:**

Using a mixed-effects model (random intercept per subject) on 19 participants who had both Rice+Fiber and Rice+Protein conditions plus SSPG clamp data:

- **Primary interaction effect:** β = 0.170 (SE = 0.064, p = 0.008), 95% CI [0.044, 0.295]

- **Tertile means:** Low-IR group: +17.2 mg/dL reduction with protein; High-IR group: -7.7 mg/dL (protein paradoxically increases peak)
